title: OpEx Week Is Starting To Get Crazy
speaker: Anthony and Shawn (Geeks of Finance)

macro_themes.view: S&P fell 1.1% after CPI into the bottom of the 7700-7800 gamma range, but probabilities stay skewed to the upside.
OpEx week often fails to follow through on trend moves, especially downside, so a VIX spike may not extend.
Treat the tech pullback as an opportunity to buy dips in strong names.

calls.reason: Flipped to slightly negative GEX at the bottom of the weekly 7700-7800 range with heavy buying at 7700; possible further decline first but upside-skewed.
calls.quote: while we view probabilities skewed to the upside, it is possible for us to retrace to the lower end of the range first.

calls.reason: VIX only spiked to low 17s and closed below the 17 negative-GEX cluster; OpEx week tends to cap follow-through.
calls.quote: I'm cautious here about seeing the VIX continue higher even if we see it trend change beyond this week.

calls.reason: Bull flag with stacked rising moving averages, positive GEX skewed to 750/800 strikes, +16M bullish flow on the dip; holds Nov 20 700/690 put credit spread.
calls.quote: in our view, this pullback is just another opportunity to get in during this consolidation period on Meta.

calls.reason: Deeply negative GEX but extreme distance below the HMA and rare -1.4B GEX reading have previously marked bottoms; expects mean reversion.
calls.quote: looking for some mean reversion here with the risk reward tilted to the upside in my view.

calls.reason: Healthy pullback to the 50-day EMA while still in positive GEX with bullish flows from 370 to mid-400s; 2026 market leader.
calls.quote: Palo Alto Networks also looking like a bargain opportunity.

notes: CPI-day close. QQQ price is the after-hours ~722-723 level. Listing date may be a day late: they mention an expired 'October 14th' put, so this may be Oct 14.
